open_questions: Ground-based photometry in QLP vs TESS-SPOC apertures to confirm on-target transit and measure true undiluted depth; multi-colour follow-up to rule out blended EB with 15.9-22 arcsec neighbours (plausible_within_1px 2) that centroid_all could not localize.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 14.9-day, 3.5-hour, 1400 ppm flat-bottomed dip consistent with a ~2.9 Earth-radius planet on this 0.66-solar-radius M dwarf. The dip looks much deeper in QLP light curves than SPOC, but that is a pipeline difference, not real changes, likely because the star is strongly spotted and variable. Centroid imaging is inconclusive, leaving a faint neighbour blend as an open possibility, but no binary signature is seen.

reasons.why: Planet-sized sub-Saturn below 10 Rearth and flat-bottom shape v_sigma -2.937; duration ratio 1.016 fits central duration for TIC rad 0.6642.

Appears highly variable, but sector_depths_by_source verdict is differs_by_source (QLP 2386±204 ppm, TESS-SPOC 363±197 ppm; per-source p_constant 0.8935 and 1.0). Difference is pipeline/aviation calibration, not astrophysical depth change, supported by stellar variability.

No difference image locates dip; by process of elimination a stellar binary is ruled out by size/shape and lack of secondary (secondary snr 3.452 <5) and RV (rv_log_p -2.947, ruwe 1.086, non_single_star 0). Two neighbours within 1px could cause dip with 0.2199 eclipse but require deep eclipses and remain unconstrained due to ambiguous centroid, so blend stays possible but not strongly favoured over on-target planet.

Star is VARIABLE phot_variable_flag VARIABLE with strong spot modulation explaining sector-to-sector depth scatter and large per-transit chi2 58.6597550610999 p_consistent 5.547e-12; no rotation-multiple lock (signal_over_rotation 2.491) and no large phase-curve signal.
